newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Three injured in Moscow car blast-Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Three injured in Moscow car blast-Interfax.

text.p: Three people were injured on Sunday when an explosion tore a car parked outside a big shopping and entertainment centre in Moscow, Interfax news agency said.

It quoted police as saying that the blast, which took place at 9.30 p.m. (1730 GMT) at a parking area near the the All-Russia Exhibition Centre, had been caused by an explosive device equivalent to 200 grams (0.5 lb) of TNT.
Interfax said the three casualties had been rushed to hospital, two of them with serious injuries.
The Exhibition Centre, a huge Soviet-era compound of shopping pavilions and entertainment facilities, was one of the key sites during weekend celebrations of Moscow's Day of the City festival.
The celebrations which usually attract hundreds of thousands of people had been dampened on Sunday by heavy rain.
It was not clear whether the blast was a terrorist attack or a mafia-style contract murder attempt which have become frequent in Moscow.
Four people were killed and dozens wounded in a series of terrorist attacks in public transport in Moscow this summer. Noone has claimed responsibility for the attacks.
